CORRECTION TO THE NOTE BELOW, WHICH WAS WRONG. It claimed 'a comment sweep moves this floor and the drop is not an improvement'. It does not move it at all, and the sentence before that claim is the reason: the gate excludes comment-only lines, so deleting a comment block shrinks the class span and the excluded count by the same N, and the excess is unchanged. Measured against a 3626-line comment sweep across addons/web and addons/point_of_sale: 7209 in a clean worktree of HEAD before and after, 0 contribution. The 7199 the shared checkout read throughout is another session's uncommitted work on webclient/home_menu, not the sweep. Kept rather than replaced because a floor that loses the record of what it once asserted costs more than a tidy note gains -- and because the wrong claim was mine, repeated to two other sessions before anyone checked it. Count unchanged at 7209; this stamp moves the note, not the floor.

PREVIOUS NOTE, kept because a floor that loses its history costs more than the stamp gains:

New gate, first floor. addons/web/static/src holds 33 classes over the 400-line budget for 7209 excess code lines, and no existing gate can see any of them: jsfunclen holds every JS function under 90 lines, and a class of short methods is invisible to a per-function budget -- the argument py_class_length.py was added for on the Python side, which had no client-side counterpart. Largest: FlowEditor 1267 over 63 methods (core/flow_editor/flow_editor.js), StaticList 1041, ListRenderer 963, CalendarModel 918, RelationalRecord 871. Unit is excess lines rather than offender count, so splitting one huge class into two large ones lowers the number rather than raising it. Comment-only lines are excluded, matching jsfunclen's eslint skipComments:true, so the two figures stay comparable -- which also means a comment sweep moves this floor and the drop is not an improvement. Measured in a clean detached worktree of fff4eb9a9f4, the commit that adds the gate, node_modules symlinked.
